title: A web rebuilt for agents can get worse for the person still browsing
friendlyTitle: A web rebuilt for agents can get worse for the person still browsing
summary: MIT Technology Review argues that personal agents, including OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, are a third kind of web visitor: not a person, and not an ordinary bot. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and one security firm says agent traffic tripled from August to September. Sites from Pizza Hut to Yelp have blocked agents. Amazon has blocked Muse and is still fighting Perplexity in court. Shopify has opened a checkout lane for browser agents. The piece asks what is left for a person who wants to compare prices themselves.

whyItMatters: If you send an agent to book a table or ask for a refund, the site may already be refusing it, or serving it a different path from the one you see. That split can help, if the agent can check a bill you would not have time to fight. It can also hide the price, the ad, and the commission. The rules for which of those is allowed are not settled. Until they are, an agent is not a reliable substitute for opening the page.
